about.title: Cloverdale Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Cloverdale is a small city, but its traffic doesn't stay small during Friday evening rush between 5 and 7 p.m., when local crash reports tend to climb. Public records show 13 injury collisions and 18 injured people in the most recent full year, concentrated along S Cloverdale Boulevard, N Cloverdale Boulevard, Cloverdale Boulevard, and the US-101 southbound corridor. Whether you were stopped at a light downtown or merging onto the highway, the aftermath of a crash brings the same questions: who pays for the ER visit, the missed work, the car repairs? LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect injured Cloverdale residents and visitors, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can evaluate the claim, deal with insurance adjusters, and explain what California law allows. There's no obligation to move forward, and no cost unless the attorney recovers money for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Cloverdale Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Starts Now
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, though claims against a government entity (like a road defect on a county-maintained street) can require notice in as little as six months. Getting connected early helps preserve options before deadlines close in.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for a Cloverdale Boulevard collision — your share of fault simply reduces the recovery rather than eliminating it. An independent attorney can help make sure fault gets assessed fairly.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in standard car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to minimize what they owe. An independent attorney can handle those communications on your behalf and help protect what you say from being used against you.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 near Cloverdale but I live somewhere else?
items.answer: Where you live doesn't determine where you can pursue a claim — what matters is where the crash occurred and where the parties involved are located. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise on jurisdiction and how to move forward whether you're a Cloverdale local or just passing through.

items.question: How long do I actually have to file a claim after a Cloverdale car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit, but if a government entity or road authority is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months for a claim notice. Because evidence like skid marks or dashcam footage fades quickly, it helps to get connected with an attorney soon after the crash rather than waiting.
